item.description: 1984 is a dystopian novel that gives us a glimpse of what society would be like without freedom of thought under a totalitarian regime. The entire world falls into endless warfare, people are persecuted, history is manipulated, and the media is filled only with propaganda. Winston Smith, a low-ranking member of the English Socialist Party, lives in suffering in a repressive world where Big Brother is always watching you and the Thought Police can read your mind. In his longing for truth and freedom, Smith embarks on a forbidden love affair with Julia, and they dare to join a secret revolutionary organization.

item.title: Alam & Berdikari
item.description: Ralph Waldo Emerson is the leader of the transcendentalist movement, an idealistic philosophy that holds that humans reach their fullest potential when they are truly independent and in harmony with nature. This book contains two important essays by Emerson: Nature and Self-Reliance. Nature outlines the foundation of transcendentalism, that reality can be understood by studying nature; self-reliance emphasizes the importance of individuality, that one should always believe in oneself.

item.title: Bhagavad Gita
item.description:
This is the only “drama of the human heart” written in a very poetic and deeply touching language. A work that is said to have existed since 500 years before Christ, beautifully encapsulating themes of divine philosophy, teachings of virtue, and universal ethical values.

Through the teachings of Krishna presented to Arjuna before the great battle of the Bharata family, known as the Bharata-yuda, readers can draw from the vast and profound content of these teachings, for our lives that are increasingly dry from the lack of spiritual waters and life wisdom.

item.title: Candide
item.description:
Translated from French. This book includes original illustrations.

Candide tells the story of a naive young man who steadfastly believes that “everything is for the best” even when faced with injustice, suffering, and despair. Controversial and entertaining, this novel is highly relevant in our world, which is filled with—as Candide puts it—“the madness of insisting that everything is fine when it is actually terrible.”

item.title: Catatan dari Bawah Tanah
item.description: “Notes from the Underground” is Dostoevsky’s most revolutionary novel. One of the most remarkable characters in literature, the unnamed narrator is a former clerk who resolutely withdraws to underground life. In complete seclusion from society, he wrote a passionate, obsessive, contradictory narrative that served as a devastating attack on social utopianism and an affirmation of essentially irrational human nature.

item.title: Civilization and Its Discontents
item.description: This important essay, which Freud worked on during the summer of 1929, is perhaps his best work ever known. This book is a brilliant overview of cultural views, from the perspective of psychoanalysis that Freud had developed since the beginning of the century. Civilization and Its Discontents (Civilization and Its Discontents, 1930) is a combination of things at once: a cursory flashback of The Future of an Illusion (1927), an analysis of the inevitable tensions that more or less make individuals enemies of society, a meditation on the lethargy that seems to be affecting so many people in modern civilization. However, this is the book of a psychoanalyst (we must remember this), and stands as a testimony and appreciation for the final theory of the soul—what is called structural theory (first revealed in Beyond the Pleasure Principle in 1920, and The Ego and the Id in 1923)—with its emphasis on acts of aggression, the impulse or stimulation of death, as Eros’s mortal enemy.

item.title: Ecce Homo
item.description:
I was the first to discover the Truth I was the first to feel with the senses -kissing lies as lies I have chosen for myself said the Immoralist as a marker of distinction and a badge of honor I am proud to have this word that prepares me against all humanity (Friedrich Nietzsche: Why I Am Destiny)

Nietszche was an extraordinary philosopher, until now his ideas are still alive even though he has been dead for more than 100 years. Philosophers who pioneered the era of postmodernism, the idea of Nihilism is very influential in the world to this day. Through his works he also overturned all values and morals. Ecce Homo’s work is the most confusing autobiographical work of existing autobigraphy writing.

item.title: Ethics: Proved in Geometrical Order
item.description: Spinoza’s Ethics is one of the most significant texts of the early modern period, important to history, philosophy, Jewish studies and religious studies. It had a major influence on Enlightenment thinkers and the development of the modern world. In Ethics, Spinoza addresses the most fundamental perennial philosophical questions concerning the nature of God, human beings and a good life. His startling answers synthesize the longstanding traditions of ancient Greek and Jewish philosophy with the developments of the emerging scientific revolution. The resulting philosophical system casts out the willing, personal God of Abrahamic religions and takes up the challenge of reconceiving the natural world and human beings in an entirely secular way. This volume offers a new translation based on a new critical edition, reflecting the state of the art in Spinoza scholarship, and also includes an introduction, chronology and glossary to help make this notoriously difficult text accessible.

item.title: Filsafat Nietzsche
item.description:
“Overall, this book is a very valuable lens into philosophy.”–Choice

Nietzsche’s Philosophy was first published in 1962 under the title Nietzsche et la Philosophie. This book showcases a rare combination of rigid scientific language and imaginative interpretation, illustrating how Friedrich Nietzsche pioneered a new way of philosophical thinking. Nietzsche’s Philosophy is one of the first books to challenge the assumption that dialectics is the sole foundation for radical thought.

Gilles Deleuze’s analysis opens an important path toward post-war thought: post-structuralism. And Deleuze also provided a new preface in the English edition translation, as the reader has in hand.

item.title: Hamlet
item.description:
Hamlet is a tragedy written by Shakespeare between 1599 and 1602, which tells the story of Prince Hamlet’s revenge against Claudius, his uncle. Claudius has killed his father and seized the throne along with the King’s wife.

One nite in the kingdom of Denmark, the guards, Bernardo and Marcellus, along with Hamlet’s friend, Horatio, suddenly encountered a ghost that closely resembled the recently deceased King Hamlet. They swore to tell Prince Hamlet about what they had witnessed.

item.title: Illiad
item.description: The Iliad roars with the clamor of arms, the bellowing boasts of victors, the fury and grief of loss, and the anguished cries of dying men. It sings, too, of the sublime magnitude of the world―the fierce beauty of nature and the gods’ grand schemes beyond the ken of mortals. In Wilson’s hands, this thrilling, magical, and often horrifying tale now gallops at a pace befitting its legendary battle scenes, in crisp but resonant language that evokes the poem’s deep pathos and reveals palpably real, even “complicated,” characters―both human and divine.

item.title: Kejatuhan
item.description: In a bar in Amsterdam, a man named Jean-Baptiste Clamence makes a confession to a stranger. He reminisces about his past life as a respected judge, has high self-esteem, adheres to libertine ideology, but is immune to the judgments—portrait of a modern human being. In the end Clamence realizes that no one is innocent, and therefore no one can judge others from the standpoint of truth.

item.title: Lahirnya Tragedi
item.description: THE BIRTH OF TRAGEDY (The Birth of Tragedy) sparked great anger when it was first published in 1871; and since then this book has become one of the books that fertilized European culture. This book, presented to Richard Wagner (great German composer, 1813-1883), was Nietzsche’s enthusiasm for Greek literature, especially his tragedy. He puts forward the difference between the Apollonian and Dionysian spirits, also emphasizing why we can enjoy tragic art, as well as what the relationship is between the suffering of life and art.

item.title: Man`s Search for Meaning
item.description: Buku ini menggabungkan kisah nyata pengalaman Viktor E. Frankl sebagai penyintas kamp konsentrasi Nazi dengan pemikiran psikologinya tentang logoterapi, yang menekankan bahwa manusia dapat bertahan dan bangkit dari penderitaan paling ekstrem ketika ia menemukan makna dalam hidupnya; melalui refleksi yang jujur dan mendalam, Frankl menunjukkan bahwa kebebasan terakhir manusia adalah memilih sikap terhadap keadaan, sekalipun dalam kondisi yang paling tidak manusiawi.

item.title: Meditations on First Philosophy
item.description:
In Meditations on First Philosophy, René Descartes leads readers into the heart of the most radical philosophical inquiry: what can we know for certain when everything is doubted? From the collapse of sensory certainty to the discovery of “I think, therefore I am,” Descartes formulated a new foundation for modern philosophy.

The six meditations he composed not only meticulously sift through doubt but also construct arguments about the existence of God, the clarity of the soul, and the fundamental difference between mind and body. The clarity of logic, equivalent to geometric proofs, makes this work a steadfast milestone in the history of Western thought.

item.title: Mitos Sisifus
item.description: The Myth of Sisyphus explores the absurdity of human existence and our search for meaning in a world that seems to lack purpose. Camus poses a fundamental question: is this life worth living? If human existence no longer has meaning, what can prevent us from committing suicide? According to Camus, if there is no God to give meaning to our lives, then it is humans who must take over that purpose themselves. This is an ‘absurd’ task, like Sisyphus who endlessly rolls his stone up the hill, while the inevitable death looms over us.

item.title: Odyssey
item.description: The Iliad and the Odyssey remain beloved stories around the world for centuries and have been translated into dozens of languages, although little is known about their author. The story of the greatness of the Greek expedition to the East and the unfortunate fates of most of its leaders had spread in Greece from generation to generation in the form of short poems for hundreds of years before the Iliad and Odyssey were composed by Homer. However, Homer did not merely combine those poems; he selected, arranged, added to, and perfected them into a final result with his genius talent.

item.title: Senjakala Berhala dan Anti-Krist
item.description:
This book is one of the phenomenal works of Nietzsche, a very popular philosopher. His works are still much sought after, this book was previously published in Bentang Budaya, best seller and printed three times in 2 years. Our other books by Nietzsche The birth of tragedy also became best sellers in Jogja stores.

The Twilight of Idols and the Anti-Christ was written in 1888, at the same time as Ecce Homo was written, an autobiography written by Nietzsche himself. But indeed Nietzsche was a controversial philosopher, he was also famous as the “murderer of God” after he announced “God is Dead” in 1883 and announced himself as Dionysius in Ecce Homo.

item.title: The Gay Science
item.description:
This book is Nietzsche’s most intimate work, presenting all the personal experiences in his struggle with the pain he received as a great gift.

It was in this book that the idea of God’s Death was first told by Nietzsche in an allegory of the Crazy Man, which was then followed by a proposition about Eternal Recurrence.

What if all philosophy until now had not stood on the stake of truth, but something else-perhaps we might call it; health, future, growth, power, life. (Friedrich Nietzsche)

item.title: The Last Messiah
item.description: The Last Messiah is a phenomenal essay by the Norwegian philosopher Peter Wessel Zapffe. In it, the philosopher reimagines the human condition as a perpetual state in which the human organism has evolved excessively and lives beyond its own biological needs due to its oversized and excessive brain.

item.title: Walden
item.description: In 1845, Thoreau moved to the woods near his hometown of Concord, Massachusetts. He lived in a cabin he built himself, on the edge of Walden Pond. Walden is Thoreau’s autobiographical work about an experiment in simple and independent living in the wilderness for two years. Thoreau believed that a life focused on essential things and in harmony with nature is more fulfilling than the pursuit of wealth.

item.title: Straw Dogs: Thoughts on Humans and Other Animals
item.description:
Straw Dogs is a philosophical work that sets out to challenge our most cherished assumptions about what it means to be human. From Plato to Christianity, from the Enlightenment to Nietzsche, Western tradition is founded on arrogant and mistaken beliefs about human beings and their place in the world.

Philosophies such as liberalism and Marxism view humanity as a species destined to transcend natural limits and conquer the Earth. Even today, despite Darwin’s discoveries, nearly all schools of thought take as their starting point the belief that humans are radically different from other animals. John Gray argues that this humanist belief is nothing more than an illusion. The aim of Straw Dogs is to explore what the world and human life would look like once humanism is finally abandoned.

item.title: Eksistensialisme adalah Humanisme
item.description:
“There is no doctrine more optimistic [than existentialism], for it asserts that human destiny lies within oneself.”

Many people will be surprised by what I have to say here about humanism. We will try to determine exactly how we understand it. In any case, let’s begin by saying that what we mean by “existentialism” is a doctrine that enables human life to unfold and also affirms that every truth and every action implies a human context and subjectivity.

item.title: Nausea
item.description:
Nausea is the story of Antoine Roquentin, a French writer horrified by his own existence. In the form of an impressionistic diary, he ruthlessly catalogs every feeling and sensation he experiences regarding the world and the people around him.

His thoughts culminate in a pervasive and intensely powerful feeling of nausea that “spreads at the bottom of a thick pool, at the very depths of our era, the age of purple suspenders and broken armchairs; it is made up of broad, soft moments, spreading to the edges, like an oil stain.”

item.title: The World as Will and Representation Volume I
item.description:
Arthur Schopenhauer’s Die Welt als Wille und Vorstellung is one of the most important philosophical works of the nineteenth century, the basic statement of one important stream of post-Kantian thought. It is without question Schopenhauer’s greatest work. Conceived and published before the philosopher was 30 and expanded 25 years later, it is the summation of a lifetime of thought.

For 70 years, the only unabridged English translation of this work was the Haldane-Kemp collaboration. In 1958, a new translation by E. F. J. Payne appeared that decisively supplanted the older one. Payne’s translation is superior because it corrects nearly 1,000 errors and omissions in the Haldane-Kemp translation, and it is based on the definitive 1937 German edition of Schopenhauer’s work prepared by Dr. Arthur Hübscher. Payne’s edition is the first to translate into English the text’s many quotations in half a dozen languages. It is thus the most useful edition for the student or teacher.

item.title: The World as Will and Representation Volume II
item.description:

item.title: Upanisad-Upanisad Utama
item.description: The Upanishads, the earliest of which were composed in Sanskrit between 800 and 400 bce by sages and poets, form part of the Vedas - the sacred and ancient scriptures that are the basis of the Hindu religion. Each Upanishad, or lesson, takes up a theme ranging from the attainment of spiritual bliss to karma and rebirth, and collectively they are meditations on life, death and immortality. The essence of their teachings is that truth can by reached by faith rather than by thought, and that the spirit of God is within each of us - we need not fear death as we carry within us the promise of eternal life.
